evidence: Single codebase with clear module separation (nodes/, src/, server/, scripts/, ui/) but no inter-service communication patterns
Core logic centralized in Python modules (Pipeline, ComfyStreamClient, FrameProcessor) with shared state and in-process execution
UI is tightly integrated with backend via aiohttp/web (server/app.py) and shared Python modules (nodes/web/)
Nodes follow ComfyUI's node-based execution model with execute(), INPUT_TYPES(), IS_CHANGED() — indicating a monolithic workflow engine
Shared tensor_cache, exceptions, modalities, utils modules used across components without service boundaries
No external service dependencies in architecture (e.g., no message queues, gRPC, REST between logical components)
Single entry points (server/app.py, example.py, benchmark.py) orchestrating the entire flow
Repository structure shows logical separation but not physical deployment separation (no Docker services, no separate repos)
risks: Tight coupling between UI, backend, and node execution may hinder independent scaling or technology evolution
Monolithic deployment increases risk of cascading failures across components
Shared state (e.g., tensor_cache, PipelineState) may cause concurrency issues under high load
Limited testability of individual components due to implicit dependencies across modules
